title: Server administration
noPermission: You don't have server admin access. Workspaces and accounts are managed by server admins.
needPassword: Server administration requires signing in on the web with a username and password. You opened this page without a password from a paired computer (cohive web), so for security you can't do admin actions here.

workspaces.empty: No workspaces yet. Create one with the form above.
workspaces.deleteMessage1: You can only delete a workspace that has no issues (drafts included), for example one created with the wrong name.
workspaces.deleteMessage2: This also deletes its invites, pending requests, services, memberships and tokens, and chat group binding. Members' accounts and devices aren't affected. This can't be undone.

new.title: New workspace
new.description: One workspace per project team. The path can't be changed after creation and appears in links and project config. You can change the display name at any time.
new.pathHint: Same rules as usernames, for example payments.
new.nameError: Use only lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, 1 to 32 characters, starting with a letter or digit.
new.displayHint: A human-friendly name, for example “Payments team”. Leave empty to show the path.
new.adminHint: Enter the username of an existing account. Leave empty to use yourself ({{self}}).

accounts.noMatch: No account starts with that prefix.
accounts.setAdminTitle: Make this account a server admin?
accounts.unsetSelfMessage: You'll lose server admin access and won't be able to open this page again. The server must keep at least one server admin.
accounts.unsetOtherMessage: “{{label}}” will no longer be able to manage all workspaces and accounts.
accounts.setAdminMessage: “{{label}}” will be able to create and delete workspaces, manage all workspaces and accounts, and deactivate anyone.
accounts.enableMessage: “{{label}}” will be able to sign in again. Their previous devices are not restored: they need to run cohive login again and wait for admin approval, and reconnect Telegram.
accounts.disableMessage: Deactivating “{{label}}” applies to every workspace they belong to: all their devices and tokens are revoked immediately, web sessions are signed out, Telegram is disconnected, and pending device requests are denied. Their memberships are kept and their issues aren't transferred automatically. Reassign them from each workspace's admin page.
accounts.unlinkDingtalkMessage: After you disconnect, group notifications in DingTalk no longer @-mention “{{label}}”, and they can't approve requests with buttons in DingTalk groups. They can reconnect from Profile.
accounts.unlinkTelegramMessage: After you disconnect, group notifications no longer @-mention “{{label}}”, and they can't approve requests with buttons in the group. They can reconnect from Profile.
accounts.label: {{display}} ({{name}})

devices.description: All pending device requests. Usually an admin of the requester's workspace approves them. If the requester isn't in any workspace, they can only be approved here.

channels.title: Chat apps
channels.description: Configure a bot token or DingTalk app credentials on the server, then restart the Cohive server to enable a chat app.
channels.none: No chat app is enabled yet, so group notifications aren't being sent (pending ones are kept).

external.title: External URL
external.description: The address teammates and coding tools use to reach the Cohive server. There is one per server. Issue links in group messages are built from it as “external URL/w/path/issues/number”. When coding tools connect through a tunnel, its hostname is automatically added to the allow list. Invite and authorization links are still generated from the address you opened the page with.
external.locked: Locked by the COHIVE_EXTERNAL_URL environment variable, so it can't be changed on the web. To change it, update the environment variable on the server and restart the Cohive server.
external.unsetWarn: Not set yet: group messages currently contain no links. The field below is prefilled with the address you're using right now. Make sure teammates can open it (it isn't localhost), then click Save.
external.hint: Protocol, hostname and port only, with no path, for example https://cohive.example.com. Leave empty and save to clear it.
external.shapeError: Enter http:// or https:// followed by a hostname (a port is allowed), with no path.
external.cleared: Cleared: group messages no longer include links.
